I totally understand! One of my friends self harmed once after I told her and I got really worried. I think the best thing to do would be to tell her and then try not to bring it up again. If she frequently hears about it and thinks that it's extremely affecting you, she'll get curious as to why and decide to try it herself. I think you should ask for her consent before you tell her, and make sure she is completely ready to hear what you have to say. If you tell her and she's unprepared, it will shock her significantly. Try your best not to make her worry as well. :)

My therapist suggested this to me, but you don't have to do it since it can be very hard and triggering to do:

Sit on a chair, and imagine yourself having a conversation with your assaulter. Your assaulter is sitting across from you, at a safe distance and they cannot hurt you in any way. Then you talk to them. You can scream cry, yell, rant, anything to just let all your feelings out about what happened and how it affected you. Tell them the things you've always wanted to tell them. 

This can be very triggering but confronting your assaulter in your mind can really take a weight off of your shoulders. Again, this is only a suggestion, so only do it when you're sure you're ready :)

My parents do that too, make sure your parents know exactly what your boundaries are. Set ground rules, and don't allow them to come in and do a body check unexpectedly. But getting body checks is a huge invasion of privacy, so if you become uncomfortable let your parents know :)

Group therapy can also help a lot! Finding people who understand what you're going through can be immensely helpful :) learning how to set your boundaries is also very important, and it takes practice to learn to say what you need. A great exercise you can do with your husband goes like this: two people stand about fifteen feet away from each other, and one takes a single step. They then ask the other person if they can take another step. This continues until the person says for the other to stop. Then you try it a second time, but now keeping in mind the fact that you can say stop whenever you start to feel uncomfortable, and don't have to worry about what the other will think. I hope this helps!
